posts.title: The Only Constants in the Middle East
posts.description: The Middle East is full of uncertainty, but two constants have shaped the region for decades: Israel is not going anywhere, and the Islamic Republic of Iran consistently overplays its hand. These two realities explain why so many attempts to normalize relations with Tehran ultimately fail. Agreements can change incentives, but they cannot change the nature of a revolutionary regime. posts.title: Democracy Is the Loser of This War
posts.description: The recent war with Iran exposed an uncomfortable asymmetry. Democracies are bound by accountability, election cycles, and the need for undeniable proof, while authoritarian regimes can absorb hardship and act on long horizons. The real casualty may be the assumption that liberal democracy is always the strongest system in a prolonged geopolitical struggle.

posts.title: Are We Crossing the 38th Parallel?
posts.description: A line drawn in 1945 split Korea into two systems that, over time, produced radically different realities. The lesson is broader: when divergence is left unresolved, it compounds. The question is whether we recognize it early, or only once it is no longer reversible.
